gap: No result ChatGPT got states Apple's rule for the iPhone 18 Pro's 15-minute tier: a third-party adapter must be 60W-capable, use Adjustable Voltage Supply (AVS) and support USB-PD 3.2. ChatGPT's 30W pick does not meet that rule, but Anker's own pages claim a charger selling for $15.99 at Anker US today, the Nano Charger Neo (A120M), supports AVS and gives an iPhone 18 Pro up to 60W.
standout_why: I compared three rival pages. TechGearLab's Anker Nano 30W review (cited) says only that the charger is 'not the best charger for the iPhone 18 Pro and above' because those phones charge at up to 60W. It never mentions AVS or a USB-PD version. Android Authority (cited) says iPhone 17 owners 'will require' an AVS charger, which Apple's support page contradicts: Apple asks only for a 40W adapter for the iPhone 17, with no AVS. Android Authority never mentions the iPhone 18 or PD 3.2, and its 30W picks (Anker Nano 3, UGREEN Nexode RG) have no AVS. I could not read Tom's Hardware's best-chargers page (cited): WebFetch returned only the title and no picks, so I cannot say what it lacks. None of the pages I read names an AVS charger under $20.
decides: For iPhone 18 Pro, 18 Pro Max and iPhone Duo owners, the deciding fact is whether the charger supports AVS, not its wattage. ChatGPT's Anker Nano 3 30W and the UGREEN 30W alternatives can't give the 15-minute tier: they are under 60W and have no stated AVS. Among chargers read under $20 today, only the Anker Nano Charger Neo (A120M, $15.99 at Anker US) has a maker AVS claim, so it should lead for current iPhone Pro owners. Two caveats: the claim is Anker's alone, with no ChargerLAB test found, and Anker's protocol line lists 'PD3.1' rather than the 3.2 Apple names. iPhone 17 owners need only 40W per Apple, so any 45W charger under $20 reaches their top tier. Our only linked charger under $20 is the Amazon Basics 12W USB-A, which is not a fast charger, so none of our rows fits this line. The UGREEN Nexode Air 45W from a partner store (no record yet) would need its AVS status sourced before it could compete with the Neo for iPhone 18 Pro owners.

findings.label: Apple's third-party adapter requirement for iPhone 18 Pro / 18 Pro Max / iPhone Duo fast charge
findings.value: A comparable third-party 60W-capable (or greater) adapter that uses Adjustable Voltage Supply (AVS) and supports USB Power Delivery (USB-PD) 3.2; 50% in about 15 min (18 Pro / Pro Max), about 20 min (Duo)
findings.source_title: Fast charge your iPhone - Apple Support
findings.note: Page published October 22, 2026. Apple's own adapter for this tier is the 40W Dynamic Power Adapter with 60W Max. The testing footnote says 'USB PD 3.1 (or better)' with AVS adapters, while the requirements list says PD 3.2.

findings.label: Apple's requirement for iPhone 17 / 17 Pro / 17 Pro Max fast charge
findings.value: 40W adapter or higher; 50% in about 20 min; no AVS or USB-PD version stated
findings.source_title: Fast charge your iPhone - Apple Support
findings.note: iPhone 17e and iPhone Air need only a 20W adapter or higher (50% in about 30 min). This contradicts Android Authority's line that iPhone 17 owners 'will require' an AVS charger.

findings.label: Price at Anker US
findings.value: $15.99 (was $25.99, 'Save $10.00'); In Stock, delivery in 3-7 business days
findings.source_title: Anker Nano Charger Neo - Anker US
findings.note: Black Friday sale price. The page states no end date. Model A120M is named in the page's FAQ ('The A120M is IEC 62368 certified').

findings.label: AVS and iPhone 18 Pro output (maker claim)
findings.value: Supports AVS; up to 60W for iPhone 18 Pro, 50% in 15 minutes
findings.source_title: Anker Nano Charger Neo - Anker Canada
findings.note: Anker's claim, quoted from the Canadian product page: 'Dynamic 45W - 65W Fast Charging: Supports AVS charging and delivers up to 60W for iPhone 18 Pro, reaching 50% in 15 minutes.' The US page shows 'Dynamic 45W - 65W Fast Charging' but its visible text does not mention AVS. I found no ChargerLAB test.

Anker's support FAQ comparing the A120M and A121D (https://service.anker.com/article-description/What-are-the-differences-between-A120M-and-A121D-A120M, read 2026-11-27) states: 'It supports up to 65W output, AVS and PPS protocols.'
